question: A project manager has two hundred pages of stakeholder interview notes and needs to turn them into a requirements draft. Which two uses of Claude fit this task? Select two.
options: A) Have Claude list where the notes contradict one another so a person resolves each conflict.
B) Have Claude supply the missing answers for the stakeholders who were never interviewed.
C) Have Claude group the interview notes into themes that the team then reviews and challenges.
D) Have Claude settle which of the requirements make the final scope, so that the debate is skipped.
E) Have Claude sign the requirements off on behalf of the stakeholders who were interviewed.
correct_answers: A) Have Claude list where the notes contradict one another so a person resolves each conflict.
C) Have Claude group the interview notes into themes that the team then reviews and challenges.
explanations: Correct. Surfacing contradictions is analysis that helps humans decide; the resolution itself stays with the people accountable for scope.
Incorrect. Inventing answers nobody gave is fabrication presented as research, and it corrupts the requirements it feeds.
Correct. Grouping a large volume of text into reviewable themes is well-specified, text-heavy work that a person still checks afterwards.
Incorrect. Scope is a decision the team owns, and delegating it removes the accountability that has to sit with a person.
Incorrect. Sign-off on behalf of stakeholders is not a task to delegate; it misrepresents people who never agreed to it.
